title: Build an LSM-Tree Key-Value Store
summary:
Build the storage engine design behind LevelDB, RocksDB, Cassandra and ScyllaDB. Writes go to an append-only **write-ahead log** and an in-memory **memtable**; full memtables are flushed to immutable, sorted **SSTable** files with a **sparse index** and a footer; reads search memtable → newest → oldest table; deletes are **tombstones**; and **size-tiered compaction** merges tables, dropping shadowed versions — and tombstones only when it is safe. A MANIFEST file is your atomic commit point, so a crash at any moment leaves a store that reopens correctly.

Interview payoff: you can explain write amplification vs read amplification, why sequential writes beat B-tree page updates on write-heavy workloads, how a torn WAL tail is detected, why compaction can resurrect deleted data if done wrong, and how this contrasts with Postgres' heap + WAL + B-tree design.

milestones.name: M1: SSTable file
milestones.description: Immutable sorted file with a binary format of your choice: records + sparse index + footer. `open` loads only footer + index; `get` reads at most one index block (checked via `bytesRead`); keys outside `[minKey, maxKey]` cost zero I/O; range `entries(start, end)`.

milestones.name: M2: Memtable + WAL
milestones.description: `put`/`delete` append to `wal.log` before touching the memtable. `open` replays the WAL after a crash, ignores a torn final record, and leaves the log appendable.

milestones.name: M3: Flush & layered reads
milestones.description: At `memtableMaxEntries` the memtable becomes a tier-0 SSTable, the WAL is emptied, tables persist across restarts, and reads go memtable → newest → oldest with tombstones hiding older values.

milestones.name: M4: Range scan
milestones.description: `scan(start, end)` merges all layers: newest version wins, tombstones hidden, half-open bounds, ascending order.

milestones.name: M5: Size-tiered compaction
milestones.description: When a tier reaches `compactionThreshold` tables, merge them into one tier+1 table and delete the inputs; drop shadowed versions; keep tombstones unless no older table remains. `compact()` merges everything. Must match an in-memory model over thousands of random ops and a restart.
